title: Finite-projective summand equations
statement:
For a finite projective $F^r$ and a displayed splitting $(i_r,p_r)$, the
arrows $\pi_{h,E,F^r}$ and $\rho_{F^r}$ are inverse and are independent of
the chosen finite-free summand presentation.

proof.text: For the coefficient functors A(X)=Rh_*E tensor^L X and B(X)=Rh_*(E tensor^L Lh^*X), the forward arrow is natural by naturality of the right-adjoint projection map. The specified reverse arrow is natural by [lem-weil-pbc-projection-inverse-coefficient-naturality]. Apply both equations to the inclusion and projection of the degree-zero splitting. Construct the finite-free strict-perfect package on the degree-zero single complex using its canonical degree-zero isomorphism and zero maps in every other degree.

Let i:M to R^N and p:R^N to M be the degree-zero maps supplied by the package, transported through the single-complex degree-zero isomorphism; i followed by p is the identity. The finite-free lemma at shift zero supplies both inverse equations on R^N. Naturality along i and p expresses the composites on M as B(i) followed by the free reverse-forward composite followed by B(p), and A(i) followed by the free forward-reverse composite followed by A(p), respectively. Replace the middle composites by identities and use functoriality and i followed by p equal to the identity. This proves both equations, including rank zero.

In the current specified-arrow construction the displayed strict-perfect package supplies only proofs of flatness and invertibility, never the underlying comparison morphisms. Its two arrow expressions are therefore definitionally unchanged when the package changes, by proof irrelevance. Reflexivity proves presentation independence; this is the same intrinsic inverse as the uniqueness calculation in the source.

proof_origin.note: Lean realization of the finite-free retract argument. Reverse-arrow naturality is proved in a separate reusable module; package independence is definitional in the existing construction.
